items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: Joe Smith and Russell. If Russell was playing first, David Fletcher, you know, Joe, too.

ctx.x: Joe Smith and Russell. If Russell was playing first, David Fletcher, you know, Joe, too. But they wasn't playing no way until they got Jabo. Jabo come in and did a whole lot, you know, that Connell Lewis music.
Mm-hmm. Did Buddy play at all?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: Even them two Smith brothers, they wasn't playing no good more than stuff in the time.

ctx.x: And when I first went to Chicago, who a lot of them fellas was playing that way? Yeah, who a lot of them? That's how Lewis got such a jump on them. Even them two Smith brothers, they wasn't playing no good more than stuff in the time.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: Woodenhead Joe, I said, no, I didn't play much tennis. What is his name? Wooden Joe.

ctx.x: Okay, well let's turn the machine off again for a second.

You never noticed how he played? Two of them, I never noticed them. All I noticed, one of them was more like Buddy and one of them was like Lewis. That's Shot, he was the one of the order of Lewis, you know, trying to play like Lewis. And Woodenhead Joe, I said, no, I didn't play much tennis. What is his name? Wooden Joe.
Well he was more of a straight man, wouldn't you? He played more lead. Yeah. It was hot, but it was lead. Yeah. Now Shot's played a lot of second, huh?
